_what_this_is: A DERIVED semantic record of the physical `main.py` under the Quantum CNS mandate. No executable implementation; replaces nothing; `main.py` is untouched.
_revision: THIRD EDITION. The second edition survived four of six challenges only in part and failed two outright. Superseded claims are kept below as audit history, per the operator's instruction — including one case where the SECOND edition's own 'acknowledged gap' turned out to be an error of search rather than a real gap. Still NOT a schema.

_adversarial_history.pass_1_2026_08_08: Five challenges, all upheld: an observer was two, a state space was missing, an equivalence class was named after an ambiguous boundary, a source-derived description passed for semantics, an exhaustiveness claim had no method.
_adversarial_history.pass_2_2026_08_08: Six challenges. Verdicts, each decided by probe before any wording changed: (1) SPLIT — the internal control quotient was still one level too coarse; (2) SURVIVES with the evidence class corrected — and the second edition had UNDERSTATED its own evidence; (3) REPRESENTATION ERROR — a hypothetical observer sat among evidenced ones; (4) SURVIVES, and the recorded 'gap' is WITHDRAWN as my own search failure; (5) REPRESENTATION ERROR — two spaces implied impossible states; (6) DOWNGRADED — static-import isolation was being read as runtime isolation.

physical_subject.body: one statement — `return run_cli()` — plus the module tail `if __name__ == "__main__": raise SystemExit(main())`

outcome_space._origin: REPLACES the second edition's two separate spaces (main_termination_mode × main_return_value). Challenge 5 was upheld: a Cartesian product of those two implies states that cannot exist — PROPAGATED_SYSTEMEXIT has no return value at all, and RETURNED has no exception code. The minimal representation that admits no impossible combination is ONE space of tagged variants, each carrying its own payload. Derived from the traced control flow, not adopted from the proposal.

variants.payload: int — the delegate's value, which the module tail then passes to SystemExit
variants.reachability: PROVEN — in-process callers observe both values

variants.payload: the SystemExit instance constructed BELOW main, carrying its own code; main has no return value in this variant
variants.reachability: PROVEN by two independent routes — argparse (--help -> 0; unknown flag / missing argument / invalid choice -> 2) and the `:quit`/`:exit` dispatcher (core route: cli/command_dispatch.py:479 raises SystemExit(0))
UNPROVEN — cli/app.py contains no exception handling, so the variant exists structurally; no probe shows it reachable in production

outcome_space.why_not_two_dimensions: Because the payload's existence depends on the tag. Storing them as independent spaces made JSON convenient and semantics wrong.

exhaustiveness_of_the_RETURNED_payload.statically_exhaustive_over_the_visible_c: 15 literal integer returns in the delegate chain (13 zeros, 2 twos); the three non-literal returns were followed — run_one_shot returns only 0, run_repl returns only 0, and `return decision.exit_code` reads a field whose producer (cli/resume.py) sets only 0 or 2 and which the caller reaches only after an `is not None` check
exhaustiveness_of_the_RETURNED_payload.NOT_runtime_proven: no probe enumerates the reachable set at runtime; ResumeDecision.exit_code is typed `int | None` and nothing confines it
exhaustiveness_of_the_RETURNED_payload.status: STATICALLY EXHAUSTIVE over today's call graph; NOT runtime-proven

observers._evidence_status_field: ADDED after challenge 3 was upheld. Placement in this section no longer confers epistemic status: every observer carries `evidence_status`, one of INSTANTIATED (a real consumer exists in the audited system) or HYPOTHETICAL_CLASS (its discrimination is conceptually known; its existence here is UNPROVEN). A hypothetical observer may describe a possible quotient and may never be cited as proof of one.

exact_exit_code_observer.evidence: test_main_public_surface.py::test_the_process_really_exits_with_the_code_main_returned — real subprocess, nothing patched, asserts returncode == 2
exact_exit_code_observer.precondition_proven: the invocation names a missing --file and fails in preflight, so the run genuinely produces a non-zero code; the test cannot pass on a run that would have exited 0 anyway

in_process_return_observer.discriminates: 0 vs 2 — and, jointly with the next observer, RETURNED from PROPAGATED_SYSTEMEXIT
in_process_return_observer.evidence: test_cli_command_precedence.py asserts main() == 0; test_cli_mode_selection.py:188 (and three further sites) assert main() == 2 on the same preflight scenario
in_process_return_observer.correction_to_the_second_edition: the second edition cited only the subprocess for the value 2 and asked whether a direct observer of `main returned 2` existed. It does, in four places. The second edition UNDERSTATED its own evidence — recorded because an audit that overstates and one that understates are the same kind of error.

in_process_exception_observer.reads: the exception type and code when main does not return
in_process_exception_observer.evidence: test_cli_argparse_surface.py wraps main() in pytest.raises(SystemExit) for the argparse routes; test_cli_command_precedence.py::test_repl_quit_propagates_system_exit_zero drives main() with a scripted `:quit` reader and asserts the SystemExit

frame_trajectory_observer.evidence_status: INSTANTIATED as a probe, not as a test
frame_trajectory_observer.reads: the trace events of main's own frame (sys.settrace)
frame_trajectory_observer.discriminates: the two internal trajectories — see internal_control_path below
frame_trajectory_observer.evidence: probe 2026-08-08; no test in the repository observes this boundary

success_failure_observer.reads: zero vs non-zero — the discrimination a shell predicate has
success_failure_observer.discriminates: coarser than the exact observer; over the currently reachable payload set {0,2} the two partitions coincide, which is a property of today's states and not of the boundary
success_failure_observer.evidence: NONE in this repository. It is described so that the coincidence cannot pass for an identity, and it may not be cited as proof of any quotient.

ast_shape_observer.reads: the source text — imports, the single definition, the tail
ast_shape_observer.class: STRUCTURAL — fires on any edit, cannot separate a deliberate change from a removed contract; not counted as behavioural protection

internal_control_path._origin: SPLIT after challenge 1 was upheld. The second edition claimed ONE class on the reasoning that `main` has no syntactic branch. That confused 'no if statement' with 'one control trajectory'. A call has a normal-completion edge and an exceptional-unwind edge regardless of syntax.
internal_control_path.boundary: the trajectory of main's own frame
internal_control_path.probe: sys.settrace over main's frame, with the externally visible process code HELD EQUAL at 0 in both runs — delegate returns 0, versus delegate raises SystemExit(0)
internal_control_path.observed: RETURNED yields frame events [('return', 0)]. PROPAGATED yields [('exception', …), ('return', None)] — the frame records an exception and its return event carries None, because no value was ever produced.
internal_control_path.quotient: TWO classes, not one: normal completion and exceptional unwind
internal_control_path.significance: the first adversarial pass corrected the state space and left the control quotient one level too coarse. Two consecutive editions asserted a quotient the file's own other section already contradicted.
internal_control_path.superseded_claim: SECOND EDITION: 'main_internal_control_path — quotient: ONE class'. Withdrawn.

value_preservation.finding: in the RETURNED variant main is an identity carrier for the payload; in PROPAGATED_SYSTEMEXIT it is a transparent conduit for the exception, code unchanged
value_preservation.evidence_returned: main() == 2 observed in-process (four sites) AND returncode == 2 observed on a real process — two independent observations of the same value at two points, which together establish transit rather than inferring it
value_preservation.evidence_propagated: probe 2026-08-08: with the delegate raising SystemExit(7), main raises SystemExit with code 7 — the transit was measured, not read off the absence of a handler
value_preservation.mutation_on_record: the process test's docstring records that dropping `return` from main leaves the tail's text guard green while a failing run exits 0

observer_dependent_split.the_pair: a real process ending via `:quit` versus one ending via EOF
observer_dependent_split.under_in_process_exception_observer: TWO classes — one raises, one returns
observer_dependent_split.recorded_per_rule_11: a class splitting as the boundary widens is expected behaviour of the analysis

returned_variant.chain: delegate return -> main return -> SystemExit argument -> process exit code
returned_variant.CAUSALITY: PROVEN — the same value observed in-process and at the process boundary
returned_variant.PROTECTION: PROVEN — the recorded return-dropping mutation is caught by the process test

propagated_systemexit_variant._origin: RE-GRADED after challenge 4. The second edition marked this chain PROVEN while also recording a gap — 'no test observes the `:quit` exception passing specifically through main'. The four questions are now answered separately, and the gap is WITHDRAWN: it was my search that was incomplete, not the suite.
propagated_systemexit_variant.chain: SystemExit constructed below main -> transits main unchanged -> process exit code
propagated_systemexit_variant.REACHABILITY: PROVEN — argparse routes and the `:quit` dispatcher, each with tests
propagated_systemexit_variant.CAUSALITY: PROVEN BY PROBE — a delegate raising SystemExit(7) makes main raise SystemExit(7); measured, not inferred from the absence of a handler
propagated_systemexit_variant.BEHAVIOURAL_OBSERVATION: PROVEN — test_cli_command_precedence.py::test_repl_quit_propagates_system_exit_zero drives main() with a scripted `:quit` and asserts the SystemExit. The second edition claimed no such test existed. It does.
propagated_systemexit_variant.PROTECTION: PROVEN — mutation QM1 wrapped main's body in try/except SystemExit: return 0, and 8 characterization tests reddened, including the `:quit` transit test and the argparse invalid-choice test. Fail-before satisfied; implementation restored; suite green.
propagated_systemexit_variant.superseded_claim: SECOND EDITION: 'gap: no test observes the :quit SystemExit passing specifically through main'. Withdrawn as an error of search.

protection_status.internal_trajectory_distinction: UNPROTECTED — only a probe observes it; no test asserts which trajectory a given invocation takes. Recorded as a fact about the suite, not as a defect: no downstream consumer of the trajectory itself has been demonstrated.
protection_status.static_import_isolation: PROVEN — see the renamed claim below

runtime_consumers._origin: RENAMED after challenge 6 was upheld. The second edition said 'isolation_from_the_runtime: PROVEN' on the strength of a test that only censuses Python imports.
runtime_consumers.what_the_test_proves: test_no_production_module_imports_from_main proves STATIC IMPORT ISOLATION: no module outside tests/ contains an import of `main`.
runtime_consumers.what_it_does_not_prove: absence of runtime consumers. A repository-visible consumer exists that no import census can see: scripts/selfcheck.ps1 invokes `main.py` as a SUBPROCESS with argv (five invocations — auto_run_dry, introspect, sweep_todo, confidence_gate and others). That consumer reads the process exit code, which makes it a real instance of the exact_exit_code_observer class outside the test suite.
runtime_consumers.withdrawn_claim: isolation_from_the_runtime: PROVEN — too strong; absence from one dependency census is not absence of all runtime consumers
runtime_consumers.unproven_remainder: dynamic import (importlib), entry-point invocation, and console-script packaging were not censused

unproven_regions.status: SOURCE-DERIVED DESCRIPTION, not certified semantics — read off the three call sites that produce 2; no observer separates 'invalid trace id' from 'file-hint preflight failure'

unproven_regions.region: runtime exhaustiveness of the RETURNED payload

explicitly_not_claimed: No identity between argparse's SystemExit codes and the RETURNED payload — the same integers in different variants of one tagged space.
No claim that the variants are equivalent because their process codes can coincide.
No design change. main being a pass-through, an identity carrier and a transparent conduit are observations.
schema_status: NOT A SCHEMA. Two adversarial passes; the first found five errors, the second found two outright failures and four partial ones — including one place where the file understated its own evidence and one where it recorded a gap that did not exist. A representation that has been wrong in both directions has not yet demonstrated stability.
